title: Number Patterns: Term-to-Term Rules and the nth Term
seo_title: Sec 1 Number patterns Worksheets: Free Secondary 1 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: recognising and representing patterns/relationships by finding an algebraic expression for the nth term
meta_desc: Free Secondary 1 sequences worksheets: next terms and term-to-term rules, finding and using the nth term, checking whether a number is in a sequence, matchstick patterns and special sequences. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: For a linear sequence, the nth term is (difference)n + (zero term). 5, 8, 11, … is 3n + 2.
key_sub: To find a term, substitute n. To test a number, solve the equation: it is in the sequence only if n is a whole number.
body_html:
How it works

A term-to-term rule tells you how to get from one term to the next, for example “add 3”.

A position-to-term rule (the nth term) lets you find any term. For a linear sequence: the number in front of n is the difference, and the number added is the zero term (the term before the first).

Example

Find the nth term of 5, 8, 11, 14, …

The difference is 3, so start with 3n.

The zero term is 5 − 3 = 2.

Answer: 3n + 2

Example

The nth term is 4n − 1. Find the 20th term.

Substitute n = 20: 4 × 20 − 1.

Answer: 79

Example

Is 50 in the sequence 4n − 1?

4n − 1 = 50 gives n = 12.75.

Answer: No, it is not a whole number

Common mistakes

  • Writing n + 3 for a sequence that goes up in 3s. It should be 3n + something.
  • Using the first term instead of the zero term: 5, 8, 11, … is 3n + 2, not 3n + 5.
  • Mixing up the position (n) and the term: the 10th term is not 10.
  • Forgetting the sign when the sequence goes down: 20, 17, 14, … is −3n + 23.

faq.q: How do you find the nth term of a linear sequence?
faq.a: Find the common difference and write it in front of n. Then add the zero term, the term before the first. 5, 8, 11, … has nth term 3n + 2.

faq.q: What is the difference between term-to-term and position-to-term?
faq.a: Term-to-term tells you how to get the next term (add 3). Position-to-term gives any term from its position n (3n + 2).

faq.q: How do I know if a number is in a sequence?
faq.a: Set the nth term equal to the number and solve. If n is a positive whole number, it is in the sequence.

items.q: The nth term of a sequence is 7n − 5. Which of these numbers is in the sequence?
items.e: 7n − 5 = 72 gives n = (72 + 5) ÷ 7 = 11, a whole number. The others do not give whole numbers. So 72.

items.q: The patterns are made from matchsticks. Which pattern uses 61 matchsticks?
Which of these is the sequence of square numbers?
items.e: Square numbers are 1², 2², 3², …: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25.

items.q: Which of these is the sequence of triangular numbers?
items.e: Triangular numbers add 2, then 3, then 4, …: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15.

items.q: What is the next term in the Fibonacci sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …?
items.e: Each term is the sum of the two before: 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: What is the next term? 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …
items.e: The differences are 2, 3, 4, 5, so add 6: 15 + 6 = 21.

items.q: Which sequence is geometric?
items.e: In a geometric sequence you multiply by the same number each time (here × 2): 3, 6, 12, 24, ….

items.q: Which sequence is arithmetic (linear)?
items.e: An arithmetic sequence goes up or down by the same amount (here − 3): 20, 17, 14, 11, ….

A sequence has nth term 5n − 2. Is 101 in the sequence?
c: No, because (101 + 2) ÷ 5 is not a whole number
items.e: 5n − 2 = 101 gives n = 103 ÷ 5 = 20.6, not a whole number. So no.

items.q: Chairs are arranged in rows. Row 1 has 12 chairs and each row has 2 more than the row before. How many chairs are in row 15?
A gym plan costs $30 for the first month and $18 for each month after that. What is the nth term for the total cost after n months?
items.e: Totals: 30, 48, 66, … go up by 18; zero term 30 − 18 = 12. So 18n + 12.

items.e: 6 hours later: 9 − 6 × 2 = −3 °C.
